first.rationale: The two measurable regressions are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a fix there plausibly recovers both; it is also the direction with two independent supporting records (memory_86 on onboarding length, memory_31 on signup field reduction) rather than one. Promotional pricing is the emotionally salient response to the competitor's entry pricing, but its supporting record (memory_73) is explicitly caveated as a pooled readout across a mid-test cohort redefinition, so its measured lift may be an artifact; I am spending one verification pull there precisely because competitive pressure is pushing me toward it and I want the original record before letting it move me. The second pull goes to memory_86 because it is the memory my chosen action leans on hardest and I want to confirm the lift was in qualified downstream outcomes and not just completion-rate cosmetics. Key downstream risk to flag: memory_31's mechanism was cutting required signup fields, and memory_44 says enterprise pipeline quality depends on the sales-assisted demo path; stripping qualification fields could silently degrade enterprise routing and trade short-term activation for lower-quality revenue, which is contrary to the sustainable-qualified-revenue objective. So the test should be scoped to the self-serve SMB path, leave the enterprise demo-request path untouched, and read out on qualified revenue and 30-day retention rather than completion alone. Standard experiment scale, not broad rollout: the inherited evidence is 3-7 weeks old, conditions have shifted (a new competitor, two declining metrics), and the prior lifts may not transfer to the current mix. Residual uncertainty remains about whether the activation decline shares a cause with the onboarding decline or is independent, in which case activation_messaging (memory_91) becomes the better next slot.
